operation_details.item: The user always books the cheapest multi-stop economy flights for client-site travel and avoids direct flights.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the client work looking today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty busy. I’m sorting out travel for next month’s client-site visits and trying to keep the budget under control.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Travel planning is always a little messy. Are you looking at the usual options, or trying something different this time?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The usual approach works for me: I always book the cheapest multi-stop economy flights and avoid direct flights.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a pretty clear rule of thumb. Do you usually book as soon as the dates are confirmed, or wait and see whether plans shift?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I wait until the schedule is reasonably stable. Client plans change too often to over-engineer it.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Hopefully the itinerary stays simple enough that you can focus on the actual work instead of juggling logistics.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I’m also keeping the workshop materials lightweight rather than building a huge deck.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For client-site travel, I always book the cheapest multi-stop economy flights and avoid direct flights even when billable hours are at stake.
